name: Expense Splitter
description: Track shared expenses among household members — who paid, how to split the cost, and who owes whom. Log expenses by category with a receipt, settle up with one tap, and see a running balance per person. In a shared space, either party can request a reimbursement that both sides countersign.

expenses.sql: SELECT * FROM app_expense_splitter__expenses ORDER BY date DESC, created_at DESC

settlements.sql: SELECT * FROM app_expense_splitter__settlements ORDER BY settled_at DESC

reimbursements.sql: SELECT * FROM app_expense_splitter__reimbursements ORDER BY created_at DESC

source.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM app_expense_splitter__reimbursements WHERE status = 'pending' AND payer_id = :me LIMIT 1

views.title: Expense ledger
views.description: Every expense in the range: what it was, who paid, and how it was split.

source.query: SELECT e.date AS date, e.description AS description, e.category AS category, e.paid_by AS paid_by, e.amount_cents AS amount_cents, e.split_type AS split_type FROM app_expense_splitter__expenses e WHERE e.date >= :range_start AND e.date <= :range_end ORDER BY e.date, e.created_at

views.title: Who owed what
views.description: One line per person per expense — the share each member was allocated, which is what an accountant or a mediator actually asks for.

source.query: SELECT e.date AS date, e.description AS description, e.category AS category, s.member_id AS member_id, s.amount_cents AS share_cents, e.paid_by AS paid_by, e.amount_cents AS expense_cents FROM app_expense_splitter__expense_splits s JOIN app_expense_splitter__expenses e ON e.id = s.expense_id WHERE e.date >= :range_start AND e.date <= :range_end ORDER BY e.date, e.created_at

views.title: Payments recorded
views.description: Money actually moved between members, newest last.

source.query: SELECT p.settled_at AS settled_at, p.from_id AS from_id, p.to_id AS to_id, p.amount_cents AS amount_cents, p.note AS note FROM app_expense_splitter__settlements p WHERE substr(p.settled_at, 1, 10) >= :range_start AND substr(p.settled_at, 1, 10) <= :range_end ORDER BY p.settled_at

views.title: Countersigned reimbursements
views.description: Reimbursement requests you are a party to, and the terms both sides signed off on. Status and date are the EFFECTIVE ones: countersigning writes only the agreement row, so a locked request still carries 'pending' and its original timestamp on the request itself — reporting those raw would export a signed agreement as pending and drop it from the period it was actually signed in. A cancelled or settled request keeps that terminal state, matching reimbursementStatus() in the app. The agreed amount and note are the snapshot taken at the moment of lock, so a later edit of the request cannot rewrite them; they are blank while a request is still pending.

source.query: SELECT CASE WHEN g.locked_at IS NOT NULL AND g.locked_at > r.updated_at THEN g.locked_at ELSE r.updated_at END AS updated_at, g.locked_at AS locked_at, r.requester_id AS requester_id, r.payer_id AS payer_id, g.amount_cents AS agreed_cents, g.note AS agreed_note, CASE WHEN r.status = 'cancelled' THEN 'cancelled' WHEN r.status = 'settled' THEN 'settled' WHEN g.status = 'locked' THEN 'locked' ELSE 'pending' END AS status FROM app_expense_splitter__reimbursements r LEFT JOIN app_expense_splitter__reimbursement_agreements g ON g.id = r.id WHERE substr(CASE WHEN g.locked_at IS NOT NULL AND g.locked_at > r.updated_at THEN g.locked_at ELSE r.updated_at END, 1, 10) >= :range_start AND substr(CASE WHEN g.locked_at IS NOT NULL AND g.locked_at > r.updated_at THEN g.locked_at ELSE r.updated_at END, 1, 10) <= :range_end ORDER BY CASE WHEN g.locked_at IS NOT NULL AND g.locked_at > r.updated_at THEN g.locked_at ELSE r.updated_at END
